scope: Puerto Rico hydrometeorological and outdoor-exposure observations and outlooks published by NOAA/NWS (and, for UV index and air quality, by EPA), frozen with byte SHA-256 provenance and bound to municipios and utility assets by recorded evidence class. Observations and outlooks are hazard context, not confirmed impact, causation or safety advice.

legacy_catalog.note: Legacy IDP-GIS metadata (ISO 19115, stamped 2020-03-12) pointing at idpgis.ncep.noaa.gov, which NWS shut down on 2023-06-30 (SCN 23-01). Live CloudGIS services are on mapservices.weather.noaa.gov. Only the Puerto Rico-relevant entries are wired here, each from its authoritative endpoint; see docs/NWS_HYDROMET_INTEGRATION.md for what was not wired and why.

sources.label: NWPS river gauges (flood status)
sources.replaces_catalog_entry: AHPS River Gauge Current and Forecast Flood Stages (ahps_riv_gauges)
sources.binding_semantics: Gauge -> USGS_<usgsId> asset by stable ID (NWPS publishes the USGS site number). Gauge -> municipio by point-in-polygon against the Census municipio boundary, corroborated by the NWPS county name; a disagreement stays UNRESOLVED.
sources.update_semantics: Bulk status every run; per-gauge detail (flood thresholds, crests, usgsId) refreshed when missing or older than detail_max_age_hours. A record revision is written only when the flood category, thresholds, service state or usgsId change; the current stage lives in data/nwps_gauge_state.jsonl.
sources.known_limits: Observed stages only: NWS issues no stage forecasts for Puerto Rico points (every forecast category is fcst_not_current). Gauges without published thresholds report not_defined and never raise a flood alert.
sources.raw_snapshot_policy: Raw response bytes under data/hydromet_snapshots/nwps_gauges/ (gitignored); byte SHA-256 committed in data/hydromet_manifestations.jsonl.

sources.label: Stage IV Puerto Rico rainfall (QPE)
sources.authority: NOAA/NWS River Forecast Centers (SERFC) via the National Water Prediction Service
sources.replaces_catalog_entry: River Forecast Centers Daily Quantitative Precipitation Estimates (rfc_dly_qpe)
sources.binding_semantics: Each municipio is summarised over the HRAP (4.76 km) cells whose centres fall inside its Census polygon (normal, departure and percent of normal over the subset of those cells that carry a PRISM normal); a municipio too small to contain a cell centre uses the cells its polygon touches (PARTIAL); no cell at all is NULL_EMPTY, never island-wide.
sources.update_semantics: One GeoTIFF per window per 12Z-12Z data day (bands: observation, PRISM normal, departure, percent of normal, inches). A re-processed file supersedes the earlier record for the same municipio/window/day. A file must carry exactly these four named bands and a data_time of 12:00 UTC on its file date, or the run fails closed. 1-day history is kept 33 days (72 h heavy-rain follow-up + 30 days of closed-alert reporting); 7- and 30-day windows keep only the latest day.
sources.known_limits: Post-event analysis published after the 12Z day closes, so it supports turbidity, inflow and landslide follow-up rather than warning. PRISM normals cover land cells only.
sources.raw_snapshot_policy: Raw GeoTIFF bytes under data/hydromet_snapshots/stage_iv_pr/ (gitignored); byte SHA-256 committed in data/hydromet_manifestations.jsonl; the dated NWPS download URL is the immutable reference.

sources.label: NWS Surf Zone Forecast (rip current risk, surf height)
sources.authority: NOAA/NWS Weather Forecast Office San Juan
sources.binding_semantics: Each product segment names its beaches ("Including the beaches of ..."); those municipios are bound by the product's own text (AUTHORITATIVE_BINDING, srf.including_beaches). Island segments with no beach line (Culebra, Vieques) bind by zone name (srf.zone_name). A coastal municipio the product never names is NOT_COVERED, never inferred from a neighbour. USVI segments are excluded and counted.
sources.update_semantics: The newest TJSJ SRF in the listing is fetched every run (WFO San Juan issues about two a day). A record revision per zone-day only when the rip current risk or surf height changes; zone-days older than retention_days are pruned whole. The current forecast per zone lives in data/outdoor_surf_state.jsonl.
sources.known_limits: Rip current risk is forecast for the two detailed periods only; extended days carry surf height alone. The product covers the beaches it names, not every coastal municipio.
sources.raw_snapshot_policy: Raw response bytes under data/hydromet_snapshots/nws_surf_zone/ (gitignored); byte SHA-256 committed in data/hydromet_manifestations.jsonl.

sources.label: NWS marine-zone alerts (Puerto Rico waters)
sources.authority: NOAA/NWS Weather Forecast Office San Juan
sources.binding_semantics: An alert is retained when it names a San Juan marine zone (AMZ7xx, frozen in data/reference/outdoor_reference.v1.json from api.weather.gov/zones). Zone -> coastal municipios: municipio polygons within 2 km of the zone polygon, computed once from the frozen zone geometry (PROXIMITY, marine_zone_within_2km); offshore zones bind to no municipio.
sources.update_semantics: The active-alert set is fetched every run. One record per NWS alert id; an alert that leaves the active set is closed by a TERMINATED revision, and closed alerts older than retention_days are pruned.
sources.known_limits: Land-zone products (High Surf Advisory, Rip Current Statement, Coastal Flood) already arrive through scripts/ingest_nws_alerts.py (area=PR) and are not duplicated here.
sources.raw_snapshot_policy: Raw response bytes under data/hydromet_snapshots/nws_marine_alerts/ (gitignored); byte SHA-256 committed in data/hydromet_manifestations.jsonl.

sources.label: NDBC/CARICOOS buoys (waves, wind, water temperature)
sources.authority: NOAA National Data Buoy Center (CARICOOS-operated buoys)
sources.binding_semantics: A buoy is an offshore point and binds to no municipio. The outdoor composer attaches the nearest buoy to each coastal municipio within 40 km of its internal point and records the distance (PROXIMITY, labelled 'nearest buoy').
sources.update_semantics: One latest-observation file for every NDBC station per run, filtered to the listed Puerto Rico stations; the current observation per buoy is rewritten into data/outdoor_buoy_state.jsonl. State only, no records.
sources.known_limits: Five stations. NDBC publishes 'MM' for a sensor that reported nothing; that is carried as null, never as calm. 41115 and 41121 are wave-only (CDIP) buoys.
sources.raw_snapshot_policy: Raw response bytes under data/hydromet_snapshots/ndbc_buoys/ (gitignored); byte SHA-256 committed in data/hydromet_manifestations.jsonl.

sources.label: EPA UV index forecast (one ZIP per municipio)
sources.authority: U.S. EPA (UV index forecast computed by NOAA/NWS Climate Prediction Center)
sources.binding_semantics: Each municipio is queried by the ZCTA with the largest land area inside it (U.S. Census 2020 ZCTA-county relationship file, frozen in data/reference/outdoor_reference.v1.json). The forecast is bound to that municipio when EPA's CITY for the ZIP names it (AUTHORITATIVE_BINDING); otherwise the row stays UNRESOLVED.
sources.update_semantics: One request per municipio per run; the current daily maximum per municipio is rewritten into data/outdoor_uv_state.jsonl. State only, no records.
sources.known_limits: A daily maximum index for one ZIP stands for the municipio. EPA's UV_ALERT flag is relative to climatology and is carried, not promoted.
sources.raw_snapshot_policy: Raw response bytes under data/hydromet_snapshots/epa_uv/ (gitignored); byte SHA-256 committed in data/hydromet_manifestations.jsonl.

sources.label: NWS gridded heat index (municipio internal points)
sources.authority: NOAA/NWS Weather Forecast Office San Juan (National Digital Forecast Database grid)
sources.binding_semantics: The grid cell holding each municipio's Census internal point (gridpoint frozen from api.weather.gov/points in data/reference/outdoor_reference.v1.json); geometry REPRESENTATIVE_POINT, evidence POINT_IN_POLYGON.
sources.update_semantics: One forecastGridData request per municipio per run; the maximum heat index and wet-bulb globe temperature over the next 24 and 48 hours are rewritten into data/outdoor_heat_state.jsonl, banded on the NWS heat-index chart. State only, no records.
sources.known_limits: One 2.5 km cell stands for the municipio. The bands are the national heat-index chart, not WFO San Juan's advisory criteria: official Heat Advisories arrive through scripts/ingest_nws_alerts.py and are what the alert layer acts on.
sources.raw_snapshot_policy: Raw response bytes under data/hydromet_snapshots/nws_gridpoint_heat/ (gitignored); byte SHA-256 committed in data/hydromet_manifestations.jsonl.

sources.label: AirNow current air quality (AQI)
sources.authority: U.S. EPA AirNow (with Puerto Rico Department of Natural and Environmental Resources monitors)
sources.binding_semantics: AirNow returns a reporting area and its coordinates per pollutant. The composer attaches the nearest reporting area to each municipio within 40 km of its internal point (PROXIMITY, labelled with the area name and distance).
sources.update_semantics: One request per query point per run, de-duplicated by reporting area and pollutant; the current AQI rows are rewritten into data/outdoor_aqi_state.jsonl. State only, no records. Without AIRNOW_API_KEY the ingest skips and writes no receipt, so the source reads NEVER.
sources.known_limits: AirNow data are preliminary and unvalidated (not for regulatory use). Needs the AIRNOW_API_KEY repository secret; built and tested against a fixture constructed from AirNow's documented response until that key exists.
sources.raw_snapshot_policy: Raw response bytes under data/hydromet_snapshots/airnow/ (gitignored); byte SHA-256 committed in data/hydromet_manifestations.jsonl. The API key is never written to a manifestation, receipt or log.
